ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 6 — Annual Wellness Visit, Subsequent — Pablo Neruda

text.paragraph: Subsequent annual wellness visit; no new complaints. [S]

Mr. Neruda returns for his subsequent annual wellness visit, with a professional Spanish interpreter; his first was with his previous physician last year. He completed the health risk assessment in Spanish beforehand. He is three weeks past his second leuprolide injection and continues apalutamide; radiotherapy to the prostate finished six weeks ago. The rash has gone. Hot flashes come four or five times a day and wake him once or twice a night; he would rather not take a medicine for them yet. His energy is lower in the afternoons, and he rests after lunch. He has no bone pain, has had no falls, and walks most afternoons. He writes every morning and has kept his official duties, apart from a week of engagements put off during radiotherapy. His interest in sex has fallen, as he was told it might; he has thought about it and does not want treatment for it now. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 2026-10-05; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

Pelvic lymph node metastases: right external iliac and right obturator nodes

Maculopapular drug rash from apalutamide, grade 2 (about 20 percent of body surface, trunk and upper arms), eight weeks into treatment; no mucosal involvement, blistering, fever, eosinophilia or liver involvement; settled on topical steroid and an antihistamine without stopping apalutamide

Subsequent annual wellness visit completed. Health risk assessment reviewed and a written prevention plan given in Spanish. Depression, alcohol, cognitive and fall-risk screens are negative. On the lipid panel from the first visit (total cholesterol 214, HDL 46, LDL 140 mg/dL), with treated blood pressure and no smoking or diabetes, the 10-year ASCVD risk by the pooled cohort equations is about 17 percent; androgen deprivation adds cardiometabolic risk. [S]
Atorvastatin 20 mg daily after shared decision; lipid panel and ALT in six weeks, with the TSH and free T4 repeat.
Next annual wellness visit in one year.

Androgen deprivation with apalutamide (Z79.899). Hot flashes, afternoon fatigue, weight gain of 2.2 kg and lower libido, all expected; mild gynecomastia; no falls; cognition normal. [S]
Keep walking and resistance exercise, which help fatigue, weight, muscle and bone.
Venlafaxine or gabapentin are available for hot flashes if he wants them.
Sexual health: the cancer center's sexual health clinic is open to him, alone or with his wife, whenever he wishes.

Hypertension (I10). 128/78 mm Hg on amlodipine 10 mg; at goal. [S]
Continue amlodipine 10 mg daily.

Follow-up: Zoster vaccine dose 1 and blood pressure check in six weeks, with a lipid panel, ALT, TSH and free T4. Medical oncology and the next leuprolide injection in nine weeks. Next annual wellness visit in one year. [S]

Voluntary advance care planning discussion of about 30 minutes, in Spanish with a professional interpreter, with his consent. He named a health care agent, and a health care proxy form was completed; the agent is recorded in the chart and is not named here. He said that what matters most to him is to keep writing, to be told the truth about his illness in his own language, and to make his own decisions. He chose not to record specific treatment preferences today and will review the plan with his oncologist and with this clinic yearly or if his health changes. [S]
